go.Chiude i launcher bloccati (Steam, Epic,: Closes stuck launchers (Steam, Epic, EA, Battle.net, Riot, Ubisoft, GOG) and clears their saved pages, the most common cause of white or black screens. Games, accounts and saves aren't touched.

go.Chiude le copie di Word, Excel e PowerPo: Closes copies of Word, Excel and PowerPoint left open in the background with no window (often the "other user" is you) and explains what to do if a coworker really has the file open.

go.Controlla che lo Strumento di cattura ci: Checks that the Snipping Tool is there and working, lets you take screenshots with the PrtScn key too, and tells you where your screenshots end up. You can undo it.
go.Controlla con cosa si aprono i file zip,: Checks what opens zip files, restores Windows' "compressed folders" if an uninstalled program broke them, and tells you what to do with password-protected zips, blocked files and names that are too long.
go.Controlla cosa rallenta i download di St: Checks what slows down Steam, Epic and Xbox downloads ("metered" network, speed limits, Windows Update, almost full disk) and clears Steam's download cache. Games and saves are not touched.
go.Controlla i programmi anti-trucchi dei g: Checks the anti-cheat programs of online games (LoL, Valorant, Fortnite, Apex, Rainbow Six…) and turns their services back on if another program turned them off. Their files are never touched.
go.Controlla il \"proxy\" (un passaggio obb: Checks the "proxy" (a checkpoint that all internet traffic must pass through): if one was left behind by a removed program and doesn't work, it turns it off (with a backup).
go.Controlla il browser predefinito, il pro: Checks the default browser, the most common problem when Outlook says "organization's policies" or does nothing. Opens the right page to choose it again (Windows doesn't let programs do this). Checks and explains.
go.Controlla il disco di sistema mentre usi: Checks the system disk while you use the PC. If it finds serious errors it tells you; it only schedules the repair at restart if you run the check on its own or from Fix a problem, never inside a cleanup.
go.Controlla il file \"hosts\" di Windows,: Checks the Windows "hosts" file, where viruses or old programs can block or redirect sites like Microsoft, Google or your bank. It only sets aside the suspicious lines, with a backup.
go.Controlla internet, i server di posta Mi: Checks the internet, Microsoft's mail servers and disk space, and tells you where the problem is. You change the account settings yourself.
go.Controlla la scheda di rete del cavo: se: Checks the wired network adapter: if it's turned off it turns it back on, if it's slow it tells you to change the cable, then restarts it and asks the router for an address again.
go.Controlla le unità di rete (Z:, S:...) u: Checks your network drives (Z:, S:...) one by one, tells you which servers respond and opens the reachable ones to reconnect them.
go.Controlla se Windows ti ha fatto entrare: Checks if Windows signed you in with a temporary profile and tells you where your real profile is: your files are usually all still there. Checks and explains.
go.Controlla se Windows è attivato e con ch: Checks if Windows is activated and with what license, and explains what to do. Tasso doesn't and never will use pirate programs to activate. Checks and explains.
go.Controlla se i dischi sono protetti con: Checks if your drives are protected with BitLocker and tells you where to find the recovery key (Microsoft or work account) before you need it. Tasso doesn't show or save the key. Checks and explains.
go.Controlla se il tasto Windows è bloccato: Checks if the Windows key is blocked by a setting and unblocks it (unless your company locked it), with a backup. It also tells you about the "Gaming" lock that many keyboards have.
go.Controlla segnale Wi-Fi, velocità del ca: Checks Wi-Fi signal, cable speed, VPN and the programs downloading or uploading in the background (OneDrive, updates). Tells you what's slowing things down. Checks and explains.
go.Controlla stato, usura e temperatura di: Checks the condition, wear and temperature of SSDs and hard drives.

ui.<b>Cosa fa:</b> Windows tiene in memoria:
What it does: Windows keeps parts of closed programs in memory "just in case", so they open faster next time. This is usually useful, but on some PCs, after hours of gaming, this memory fills up and the game starts to stutter. The button clears it.
When it helps: only if a game runs fine at first and stutters after a long time. Windows then fills it up again by itself, and that's normal.
Risks: none; for a few minutes programs open a little slower.
ui.<b>Cosa fa:</b> Windows, senza dirtelo,:
What it does: Windows quietly keeps recording the last few minutes of your game so you can save a "clip". This takes a bit of power from the graphics card. With the switch on, the hidden recording stops.
When it helps: always, if you don't use Windows clips (Win+Alt+G). Gain: a few more FPS on less powerful PCs; if recording was already off (this happens often), nothing changes.
Risks: none. OBS, Medal, NVIDIA and AMD keep recording normally.
ui.<b>Cosa fa:</b> dice a Windows \"quando:
What it does: tells Windows "when a game is open, give it priority" on the processor and graphics card, ahead of background programs (updates, browser, Discord).
When it helps: if you have other things open while you play and notice small stutters. Gain: honestly small: Windows 10 and 11 already do this fairly well on their own. It can only help on low-power PCs with lots of things open.
Risks: none: background programs just run a bit slower while you play.
ui.<b>Cosa fa:</b> fa funzionare i giochi i:
What it does: makes games in windowed and "borderless fullscreen" mode work almost like true fullscreen.
When it helps: if you play in a window or borderless (handy for switching to your browser or Discord). Gain: less lag and sometimes a few more FPS.
Risks: none. Windows 11 only.
ui.<b>Cosa fa:</b> la scheda video organizz:
What it does: the graphics card organizes its own work instead of being told what to do every time by the processor. The processor has less to do and the image reaches the screen sooner.
When it helps: with recent cards: NVIDIA GTX 10 or newer, AMD RX 7000 or newer, Intel Arc. It's needed for "Frame Generation" (DLSS 3, AFMF). Gain: a little less lag.
Risks: in some old games it can cause small stutters: if so, turn it off. Takes effect after you restart the PC; on old cards Windows ignores it.
ui.<b>Cosa fa:</b> normalmente Windows aspe:
What it does: normally Windows waits a moment and sends data in small batches to save resources. For an online game, it's better for every action (shot, jump, movement) to go out right away. With this, Windows sends everything as soon as it can and doesn't hold the network back.
When it helps: in online games, especially slightly older ones. Gain: a few milliseconds less, but only in games that use this type of connection (mostly MMOs and older games). Modern shooters usually don't, and there nothing changes. Your internet ping doesn't change: that depends on your provider.
Risks: none. Takes effect the next time you start the game.
